hypotheses.claim: Output-only translation validation is insufficient for effectful lowering; a transform can preserve returned values while deleting, duplicating, reordering or bypassing effects/authority checks.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production-language proof/test shows returned-value equality entails all externally observable effect/outcome equivalence for the admitted effect surface.

hypotheses.claim: Exact total effect-trace equality is a safe conservative BASE oracle but is unnecessarily restrictive for effects on proven-disjoint resources.
hypotheses.falsifier: Frozen ClayCode semantics intentionally make total source order of all effects observable even across disjoint resources.

hypotheses.claim: ClayCode lowering should represent effect-dependency/order separately from capability authority; ordering constrains transforms but never grants authority.
hypotheses.falsifier: A simpler production mechanism proves equivalent transformation safety, replay and authority closure across all BASE targets without an explicit dependency/order plane.

hypotheses.claim: A flat transitive effect set is insufficient for optimization legality; resource/order-domain identity and operation phase are needed to distinguish conflicting from commuting effects.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production alias/resource analysis derives every required conflict fact without enriching semantic/lowering effect identity.

hypotheses.claim: Optimizer/pass provenance and optimized-IR/artifact hashes belong in translation receipts but should not rewrite source canonical semantic identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: A concrete BASE replay/cache requirement proves optimizer configuration is part of source semantic identity.

hypotheses.claim: Authority checks, reserve/commit/rollback and error/re-entry boundaries are non-speculatable by default.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production effect class is proven speculatable without changing denial, outcome, durable state, replay or re-entry observations.

hypotheses.claim: Current pure evaluator versus C lowering likely diverges on short-circuit: evaluator paths eagerly evaluate both operands while C lowering preserves &&/|| short-circuit; a recursive/trapping RHS should discriminate it.
hypotheses.falsifier: Current-checkout regression shows evaluator and backend agree for false&&diverging_RHS and true||diverging_RHS, or the inspected path has been superseded.

counterhypotheses.claim: BASE should avoid Clay-level optimizer complexity and use conservative direct lowering until release.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Compare BASE acceptance/performance with no Clay optimizer and explicit backend effect conservatism.

counterhypotheses.claim: Backend compiler side-effect semantics are sufficient; ClayCode IR needs no explicit effect-order plane.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Prove identical effectful Python/C/native behavior and replay under optimization without Clay-level order metadata.

counterhypotheses.claim: Exact total effect trace equality should remain the permanent contract.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Measure whether safe disjoint-resource reordering yields material concurrency/latency gains without replay loss.

counterhypotheses.claim: Effect sets plus runtime alias/resource analysis are enough; resource identity need not be in semantic/lowering IR.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Ask the optimizer to prove same-resource versus disjoint-resource reordering using only current IR metadata.
